headline: Hiring struggles. Nuclear batteries tested. Space budgets swell.
deck: The space industry grapples with talent shortages while funding flows.

stories.head: Space sector faces talent acquisition woes
stories.body: The space industry is caught in a bind between ambitious hiring goals and its historical challenges, as highlighted by a recent report. With companies like SpaceX and Blue Origin competing for the same talent pool, many firms are finding it hard to attract engineers despite the sector's growth. This is a classic case of 'not enough talent for too many rockets.'
stories.soWhat: If the talent drought continues, we might see even more delays in projects that are already running behind schedule.

stories.head: Startup tests nuclear battery in orbit
stories.body: A startup is currently testing a tritium-powered nuclear battery in orbit, a move that could provide satellites with a reliable power source during dark periods. This initiative comes as the commercial space sector looks for sustainable energy solutions, with funding from private investors amounting to $50 million. If successful, this could change the power dynamics of satellite operations.
stories.soWhat: If this battery tech works, we might see a rush of satellite operators looking to ditch solar panels for something more reliable.

stories.head: True Anomaly raises $190M amid defense pull
stories.body: True Anomaly secured $190 million in a Series C funding round, bringing its valuation to $1.6 billion. This investment underscores the increasing demand for co-orbital security and space domain awareness solutions, with the Department of Defense showing a keen interest in the startup's capabilities. It's clear that the DoD sees the value in having more eyes in the sky.
stories.soWhat: The heavy defense pull suggests that the market for space security is heating up, and companies not in the game might find themselves left behind.

watchlist.title: ElevationSpace's reentry vehicle progress
watchlist.body: Keep an eye on ElevationSpace as they advance their commercial reentry vehicle work, potentially setting the stage for competition with established players like SpaceX.

watchlist.title: Palantir's TITAN program extension
watchlist.body: Palantir's $480 million extension on the TITAN ground station program indicates a strong government appetite for data-driven solutions, which could lead to more contracts.

watchlist.title: Anduril and L3Harris collaboration
watchlist.body: The partnership between Anduril and L3Harris for a tactical SDA constellation bid could reshape the landscape of space situational awareness, so watch for developments.

watchlist.title: Hypersonic glide-vehicle tests delayed
watchlist.body: With another hypersonic glide-vehicle test slipping, the implications for defense readiness and funding priorities are worth monitoring closely.

talent.statLabel: Job orders YoY · plus 2 starters per head, an 8-year first
talent.head: Demand has doubled. So has our hit rate.
talent.body: EVONA's job orders are up 2.0× year-over-year, and for the first time in our eight-year history we're placing two new starters per EVONA staff member. The first number says demand is real. The second says we're converting it, which in recruitment is the only number that actually matters. Growth is heaviest in Series B/C startups; primes are running flat. Compensation isn't the variable. The constraint is schedule risk in the primes: senior engineers leave Boeing, Lockheed, Northrop because they want to ship hardware before retirement.
